exposure: Supported Diagonal Flexion (SDF) positioning during skin-to-skin contact (SSC)
outcome: Quality of mother-very preterm infant communication
Infants' state of consciousness (Assessment of Preterm Infants' Behavior scale)
Onset and duration of infants' smiles, gazes, and vocalizations
Onset and duration of mothers' smiles, gazes, and vocalizations
Temporal proximity of mother-infant communicative behaviours
cohort: The study included 34 mothers and their very preterm infants (27 to 31 + 6 weeks GA) assigned to either the SDF Intervention or Vertical Control positioning group during skin-to-skin contact.
finding: Supported Diagonal Flexion (SDF) positioning during skin-to-skin contact fostered greater opportunities for mother-infant communication, including increased infant vocalizations, greater maternal vocalizations, gazes, and smiles, and enhanced multimodal temporal proximity of behaviors compared to Vertical Control positioning.
cross-section timing: Data was collected during the first 5 minutes of SSC, 15 days after the very first SSC (i.e., 18 days after very premature birth, at an average of 32.4 weeks GA).
gest_age: 27 to 31 + 6 weeks GA (mean age at birth 30 weeks GA)
